1: Power centres on a strong personality; when he weakens it moves down or sideways. A State is the organisation that rules land and people through L, E, J.
Fifteen Mughal monarchs, Babur 26-30 to Bahadur Shah Zafar 37-57, pass the baton by reign codes. Only Humayun 30-40 has two reigns. Mughal State: 1526-1858, break 1540-55.
Babur 26-30, born 1483 in Fergana, lost it by 1512; Kabul (1504) was poor. India was rich but weak under the Lodis, so he attacked from 1519 with Ottoman gunners.
Babur 26-30 had about 12,000 men but small bronze cannons. Ibrahim Lodi was killed at Panipat 1526. The Delhi Sultanate (1206-1526) ended; a Mughal kingdom, not yet an empire, began.
Humayun 30-40 lost to Sher Shah 40-45 Suri 40-45 at Chausa (1539) and Kanauj (1540); Suris ruled 1540-55. Sher Shah's Patta-Qabuliyat, Rupiya and Grand Trunk Road outlasted him.
Safavids helped for a price: Shia forms, Kandahar, Persian culture. Humayun 30-40 won at Sirhind (1555), then died in 1556 falling from his stairs. Bairam Khan beat Hemu for Akbar 56-05.
Akbar 56-05 built Mansabdari: each Mansabdar held a mansab, Zat plus Sawar rank, paid in cash or Jagir. Lineage beat merit, Birbal excepted. Tankha Jagir was transferable; Watan Jagir hereditary.

Owner, tenant, collector and State all hold rights in land. The State assessed through Patwari, Qanungo, Amil, Amalguzar, settled by Patta and Qabuliyat, collected via Zamindar (about 10%) and Muqaddam.
Mansabdari was a patron-client bond: rank and Jagir for loyalty and an army. Loyalty was personal, so after 1707, if the King could not deliver, it dissolved. Army: 2 lakh paper, 1 lakh real.

When the treasury ran short, Ijaradari auctioned collection to an Ijaradar paying in advance for 3 to 5 years. Akbar 56-05 practically abolished it; weak rulers revived it until Warren Hastings 73-85 made it the Farming System, 1772.
To hold a diverse realm Akbar 56-05 moved from Ibadat Khana (1575) to Mahzar (1579) to Din-i-Ilahi (1582), all resting on Sulh-i-Kul. Jizya: first Muhammad bin Qasim, then Qutb-ud-din Aibak 06-10.
2: In 1707 Aurangzeb 58-07 ruled the biggest Mughal State, yet economic and social power had not peaked. All five powers would weaken together. He laid the foundation of decline; weak successors added to it.
Aurangzeb 58-07 (1658) wanted the Deccan: Bijapur 1686, Golconda 1687. Marathas never submitted. About 40 years of war drained treasury and Mansabdars; by 1705 Marathas were winning.

Aurangzeb 58-07 followed orthodox Islam: Jizya re-introduced 1679, Kashi Vishwanath demolished 1669. He executed Guru Tegh Bahadur (1675) and Sambhaji 80-89 (1689), who became martyrs and hardened Sikh and Maratha feeling.
Mansabdari ran on personal loyalty and give-and-take. A strong emperor kept an unhappy Mansabdar quiet; a weak one could not, so nobles lobbied, backbit and plotted a takhtapalat.

Europeans won with file firing, grapeshot and bayonets; Haider Ali 61-82 reformed, the factional Mughals did not. Court politics, not merit, chose commanders, and Mansabdars kept fewer cavalry than their Sawar rank.

Mansabdars rose while land shrank, like a water crisis. After 1686-87 Khalisa grew yet Deccani nobles came in; later Mughals over-recruited. 5% of Mansabdars held 61% of Jagir revenue. Teacher: most important cause.

Jagirs were shuffled, so no Jagirdar felt safe and each extracted the maximum fast. Ijaradari spread; Zamindar revolts followed, like Churaman 95-21 Jat in 1695. Corrupt armies lost to rebels and Nadir Shah.
Five court factions fought. Farukhsiyar 13-19 refused to be a Sayyid puppet; Sayyids and Marathas (1719) killed him and installed Muhammad Shah 19-48. Nizam-ul-Mulk 24-48 took Hyderabad, 1724.
From 1705 Marathas beat Mughal forces. In 1737 Peshwa Bajirao 20-40 plundered Delhi; in 1738 they beat the Nizam's army, and the Treaty of Bhopal gave Chambal-Narmada lands and Malwa.
Nadir Shah wanted plunder. Karnal routed the Mughals; Nizam bought peace for Rs 50 lakh, but snubbed Sadat Khan 22-39 goaded Nadir to Delhi. 60 days, 2 lakh dead, 100 crore looted, Peacock Throne.
After Nadir Shah came Abdali's first invasion, 1748. In 1752 the emperor came under Maratha protection; in 1754 they installed Alamgir II 54-59. Many States replaced one; Marathas were No. 1.
Prelims 2003: Shah Alam II 60-06 feared his Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk, not invaders. Mains 2017: find the protagonist, weight 30% Mughal decline and 70% regional powers; flip if the Mughals are the subject.
3: Control can exist without rule (absentee colonialism, Angola and Mozambique). Rule means L, E, J plus governance. For the EIC in Bengal, Plassey 1757 was control, Buxar 1764 was rule.

By the mid-18th century the Mughal State no longer worked as one. From 1707 to 1800 power spread into Successor, Rebel and Already Autonomous States; Successor States arose under FS 13-19 and Md Shah 19-48.
Murshid Quli Khan (MQK 17-27) set up Bengal in 1717, Sadat Khan 22-39 Awadh in 1722, Nizam-ul-Mulk 24-48 Hyderabad in 1724. All ruled as sovereigns; none declared independence, for four reasons.
Akbar 56-05 split a province in three: Subahdar the Sword, Diwan the Purse, Bakshi the Eyes. Each reported to a different Delhi officer, bypassing the Nazim: checks and balances.

Founders broke that design: take the Subahdari, replace checks with loyalists, build revenue, co-opt men of money, turn Tankha into Vatan Jagirs. Result: a Nawab over a network, Mughal link kept as symbol.

In 1717 MQK 17-27 became Nazim while already Diwan, ending Akbar 56-05's checks. By 1727 fifteen Zamindars collected 50% of LR, funded by the Jagat Seths. Alivardi Khan 40-56 toppled Sarfaraz Khan in 1740 with their backing.
Raghuji Bhonsle raided Bengal 1745-51; the 1751 settlement gave him Chauth and Orissa. Alivardi stopped paying Delhi. Successors followed, and in 1765 the Diwani passed to the EIC.
Sadat Khan 22-39 got Awadh in 1722, then urged Nadir Shah to Delhi in 1739 after being passed over. Safdar Jung 39-54 resigned in 1753; Shuja 54-75 lost at Buxar (1764); Awadh annexed 1856.
Nizam-ul-Mulk 24-48 helped remove the Sayyids, took Hyderabad in 1724, lost to the Marathas in 1728 and 1738, then gave up on Delhi after 1739-40. Coins and Khutba kept the emperor's name.

The Hyderabad Subah had a southern part, the Carnatic, with its own Nawab under the Nizam. Saadatullah Khan made the post hereditary, Dost Ali Khan was killed in 1740, Anwar-ud-din Khan became autonomous too. Prelims 2021 trap.

In all three, a strong Mansabdar gathered power and none declared independence. The Carnatic was a State inside a State. The emperor became a constitutional monarch; legitimacy and real power split, opening the door to the EIC.
